GF64: a double

You will learn

The 64-bit GoldenFloat, 1 + 24 + 39, beside IEEE double, and how its encoder clamps the exponent.

GF64 has 64 bits: 1 sign, 24 exponent, 39 mantissa, bias 8388607. IEEE double spends 11 bits on the exponent and 52 on the mantissa; GF64 trades mantissa for a far wider range. Its spec has an encoder and a decoder: the mantissa divides by 2^39, and the exponent is clamped between 0 and 2^24 - 1.

Try it

Find EXP_BIAS, EXP_MAX and MANT_DIV in gf64.t27. Then open encode and find where the exponent is clamped.
